thread:
olivia (support): FYI customer reporting intermittent 503s + KMS failures after our scheduled KMS rotation in their private VPC. They say it started ~10:30am local.
sam (eng-security): Can you paste the exact error payload they saw? 503 from our API or KMS 403? :thinking:
olivia (support): Here's the snippet from their app logs:
```
POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate 503 Service Unavailable
{"error":"kms:access_denied","detail":"failed to fetch wrapped key: connection reset"}
```
They also attached a tcpdump showing SYN->RST to our KMS endpoint IP when from the customer's gateway.
li (eng-infra): Important detail: this is Private deployment with customer-managed NAT + stateful firewall. We saw KMS rotation at 10:15 and pushed new endpoint certs. Could be asymmetric routing or hairpin NAT during rotation.
amir (solutions): Customer says their FW is default-deny outbound except allowlist to our API and KMS. They added our new KMS IP range per rotation email but still failing.
olivia (support): Customer checked, they allowed 35.201.10.0/24 (old) and 35.209.99.0/24 (new token) — we gave them both. Still seeing conn reset.
sam (eng-security): Quick checks: 1) Is our KMS endpoint resolving to multiple AZ IPs? 2) Did cert rotation change SNI expected hostname? 3) Any MTU or TCP MSS clamping causing resets?
li (eng-infra): KMS endpoints are behind regional NLBs; IPs can change mid-rollout. SNI didn't change (still kms.redwood.internal). But NAT hairpin can cause reply path to go to a different egress IP not allowed by their allowlist.
olivia (support): They ran `curl -v` from a host behind their NAT and got:
```
* Connected to kms.redwood.internal (35.201.10.17) port 443 (#0)
* TLS handshake... server certificate OK
* POST /v1/wrapkey -> Connection reset by peer
```
And when they traceroute'd we saw return path jump to a different egress IP.
amir (solutions): This screams asymmetric return path + stateful FW killing connection when reply comes from unexpected source. If the NAT maps by connection tracking to egress IP A but reply arrives to egress IP B, firewall drops/RST.
sam (eng-security): Agreed. Mitigation options for customer: 1) widen egress allowlist to include all regional egress CIDRs during rotation window, 2) use a proxy in their VPC pinned to a single IP, or 3) enable sticky egress (if their infra supports it).
li (eng-infra): Also add note: if they use SNAT with multiple NAT gateways behind a load balancer, ensure source persistence or avoid ephemeral egress IPs during cert rotations.
olivia (support): Customer wants a reproducible repro steps set to show their security team. Can we give a small script + tcpdump snippet they can run to demonstrate asymmetric egress effect?
sam (eng-security): Sure. Suggestion to send them:
```
# from inside their VPC host behind NAT
sudo tcpdump -i any host kms.redwood.internal -w /tmp/kms-trace.pcap &
for i in {1..10}; do curl -sv https://kms.redwood.internal/v1/wrapkey -d '{"kid":"test"}' || true; sleep 1; done
sudo pkill -f tcpdump
# show unique src IPs observed in packet captures
tshark -r /tmp/kms-trace.pcap -T fields -e ip.src | sort | uniq -c | sort -nr
```
Explain to them: if you see responses from multiple src IPs not in your allowlist, that's the issue.
amir (solutions): Also include a quick `iptables -S` snippet for them to paste so we can confirm stateful conntrack limits:
```
sudo iptables -S
sudo conntrack -L | head -n 50
```
olivia (support): I'll send that repro and recommendation (widen allowlist temporarily) and ask them to try pinning egress. Any security concerns with asking them to open wider egress during rotation? we should recommend least-privilege windows.
sam (eng-security): Recommend: 15-30 min maintenance window, widen to regional egress CIDR, monitor for failures, then tighten back. Log the change in their change control. Also we should add a note for our rotations: publish expected intermediate egress CIDR list and advise customers with strict NATs on patterns.
li (eng-infra): I'll file an internal action item to add a short paragraph to rotation emails about NAT hairpin/asymmetric routing and recommended mitigation. @infra-bot can you create a jira? :robot_face:
infra-bot: Created REDWOOD-9764 "Update KMS rotation docs: NAT hairpin and egress guidance" assigned to li (eng-infra).
olivia (support): Thanks everyone. I'll loop customer in, run repro, and post results here. :thumbsup:
sam (eng-security): If they still see `kms:access_denied` after widening, capture full TCP dump and we can check for TLS alert messages or RST patterns.
olivia (support): Will do. Closing for now until they run repro. Posting results later in thread.
